changes.title: Crude fell more than 7 percent on Monday on a strengthened diplomatic signal, and December WCS widened back through $30 on traded volume
changes.delta: Monday settles: Brent Jan27 $104.77, down $8.66 or 7.63 percent; WTI Dec26 $96.46, down $7.66 or 7.36 percent (Reuters), biggest one-day percentage decline since July. Overnight Brent $105.25 at 0104 GMT, up 48 cents, on a reported US strike on Qeshm Island, flat by 0355 GMT. December WCS -$30.69 (ICE TMW settle, Nov 2) on 475 lots. ARV to TMW December spread +$7.66. Diesel crack $93.10 on the validated history. November apportionment Light 19 percent and Heavy 7 percent at Kerrobert in effect.
changes.body: Brent Jan27 settled at $104.77 on Monday, down $8.66 or 7.63 percent from Friday's $113.43 settle, and WTI Dec26 settled at $96.46, down $7.66 or 7.36 percent (Reuters), after Iran's president said the Supreme Leader had granted the government authority to pursue peace talks and the US president cast doubt on resuming strikes. Overnight Brent was up 48 cents to $105.25 at 0104 GMT on a Wall Street Journal report, citing US officials, of a US strike on Iran's Qeshm Island, and was flat by 0355 GMT. Iranian negotiators left Doha on Sunday, a draft proposal is being shared, and Qatari mediators travelled to Tehran on Monday night. No agreement exists and the loadings gauge west of Hormuz holds at about 11 million barrels a day. December WCS is -$30.69 (ICE TMW settle, Nov 2) on 475 lots, widening 94 cents, and November Mainline apportionment (Light 19 percent, Heavy 7 percent at Kerrobert) is in effect. The validated diesel crack is $93.10 on the Nov 3 print.
changes.balance: The diplomatic signal strengthened without moving a barrel: a negotiating mandate described by Tehran's president, mediators in Tehran, and presidential doubt about resumed strikes in Washington took more than 7 percent off both benchmarks, while loadings held at about 11 million barrels a day. The move is a premium repricing until an accepted agreement or a flow print makes it a supply event. In Canada the traded differential widened on volume the same day, so the basin's egress and freight position did not soften with flat price.
changes.conditional: A published acceptance with terms would start the two day reopening sequence and make the channel a supply event. If the channel stalls after the midterms and the price does not recover toward the $113.43 January settle, Monday's move was positioning rather than a talks effect.
changes.source: Reuters, Nov 2-3, 2026; Wall Street Journal via Reuters, Nov 3, 2026; ICE Report Center EOD, Nov 2, 2026; validated crack history refreshed Nov 3, 2026; Enbridge apportionment notice, Oct 20, 2026

changes.title: Gibson Energy printed record third quarter results and sanctioned the Chauvin pipeline expansion
changes.delta: Gibson Q3 (Nov 2): record consolidated adjusted EBITDA C$193 million, record Infrastructure adjusted EBITDA C$177 million, Marketing C$35 million. Chauvin expansion sanctioned: system capacity up approximately 50 percent, in service first half of 2028.
changes.body: Gibson Energy released third quarter results on Nov 2 after the close: record consolidated adjusted EBITDA of C$193 million and record Infrastructure adjusted EBITDA of C$177 million, driven primarily by a full quarter of contributions from the Chauvin infrastructure assets, and Marketing adjusted EBITDA of C$35 million. The company sanctioned the Chauvin pipeline expansion, which will increase system capacity by approximately 50 percent, supported by strong commercial interest and growing production in the Mannville, with an expected in-service date during the first half of 2028.
changes.balance: The expansion is gathering-side capacity growth behind rising Mannville production: it supports basin supply growth in 2028 and does not change prompt egress, which remains set by Mainline apportionment and Trans Mountain nominations.
changes.conditional: Construction timing or a change to the first half of 2028 in-service date would move the supply-support read; prompt diffs do not price this item.
changes.source: Gibson Energy third quarter 2026 results, Nov 2, 2026 (GlobeNewswire)

changes.title: Reserves: a direct check on Nov 3 finds no new posting, and the heating oil award remains open
changes.delta: No change since the Nov 2 direct check: newest reserve item remains the Oct 29 announcement; award sheets unchanged; heating oil reserve award still not posted (deliveries due Nov 13).
changes.body: Checked directly on Nov 3, the Energy Department's newest reserve item remains the Oct 29 announcement completing the 172 million barrel commitment, and no new solicitation, award or changed award sheet has posted since the Nov 2 check. No award document has been posted for the Northeast heating oil reserve exchange; deliveries under it are due by Nov 13.
changes.balance: The reserve programme is fully awarded and unchanged, so its remaining content is scheduling: deliveries out through December, and from early next year the return of more than 216 million barrels, 44 million of it premium barrels. The one open item is the heating oil reserve exchange, whose delivery deadline is Nov 13 with no award document posted.
changes.conditional: A posted heating oil reserve award closes the last open reserve item. Any change to the posted award sheets, or a delivery schedule from the Department, updates the return timing.
changes.source: US Department of Energy newsroom and Award Information sheets, checked directly Nov 3, 2026

flags.title: Hormuz: a strengthened diplomatic signal, a draft being shared, no acceptance, and a reported limited strike on Qeshm Island
flags.body: Iran's president said the Supreme Leader had granted the government authority to pursue peace talks. Iranian negotiators left Doha on Sunday and a draft proposal is being shared; Qatari mediators travelled to Tehran on Monday night. Iran's foreign ministry confirmed the reopening plan could now be implemented within two days while restating that the US naval blockade must end first. The US president cast doubt on resuming strikes and indicated a deal remained possible; Washington has not accepted the plan. The Wall Street Journal reported a US strike on Qeshm Island citing US officials, with no flow effect reported. Crude fell 7.63 percent in Brent on Monday and barely bounced overnight. Preliminary October loadings west of Hormuz ran about 11 Mb/d against 14.5 before the war (Vortexa via Windward, Oct 29). Trade the loadings, not the communique count.
flags.trigger: A published agreement with accepted terms, a tier one flow print stepping away from about 11 Mb/d in either direction, or a confirmed escalation beyond the limited-strike pattern

flags.title: December apportionment: the nowcast is persistence at 19 and 7, no judgment call is registered, and nominations close Nov 17
flags.body: November Mainline apportionment (Light 19 percent, Heavy 7 percent at Kerrobert) is in effect from Nov 1. December's outlook opens at persistence on those levels. The evidence pack for a December call now includes two traded December widenings in three sessions (-$31.10 on Oct 28 and -$30.69 on Nov 2, the second on 475 lots) against one tightening print, the export spread at +$7.66, and a flat price flush that touched no Canadian physical fact. December nominations close Tuesday Nov 17; an unregistered call after that date is a lost data point for the prediction record.
flags.trigger: Registration of a December judgment call, the Enbridge December apportionment notice in mid November, or a material change in the November physical backdrop

flags.title: December WCS has traded wide twice in three sessions: Friday's tightening is graded unconfirmed
flags.body: December WCS settled -$29.75 on 990 lots on Oct 30, a tightening print, then -$30.69 on 475 lots on Nov 2, a widening of 94 cents, after settling -$31.10 on Oct 28. Two traded widenings against one traded tightening is the graded pattern for the front: the front is wide on traded evidence, and the next traded December print on the strong side of -$30 is what would change the grade.
flags.trigger: The next traded December TMW print, or a traded ARV print replacing the current zero-volume December mark

calendar.title: Suncor Q3 results (after market close); US midterm elections; API weekly data
calendar.impact: Suncor's release is the check on its Edmonton and Base Plant fall-work completion and the guided Base Plant Q4 maintenance item. The midterms and the expiry of the strike moratorium tied to Nov 3 are the dated hinge for the diplomatic channel, and the API figure opens the weekly inventory sequence.

calendar.title: EIA weekly petroleum report, 10:30 a.m. ET; Cenovus Q3 results; Suncor webcast; ST3 refresh
calendar.impact: The weekly inventory print for the week ending Oct 30 in its standard slot; no forward forecast from the major bank weekly note was found in its usual public republication channel, so the triangle runs on the API figure and the published surveys. Cenovus reports the same morning, and the PADD 2 utilisation line arbitrates the Midwest recovery. The monthly ST3 refresh also runs and is expected to close the September gap.

calendar.title: Enbridge Q3 results (before open)
calendar.impact: Enbridge is the egress system's operator reporting into the apportionment season.

calendar.title: US-hosted Ukraine and Russia talks, Abu Dhabi (Nov 10-11)
calendar.impact: A dated diplomatic event on the second war theatre; any agreed de-escalation steps would reprice Russian barrel risk, and none has been agreed.

calendar.title: Northeast heating oil reserve delivery deadline
calendar.impact: Deliveries under the heating oil reserve exchange are due by Nov 13; no award document has been posted as of Nov 3.

calendar.title: December Mainline nominations close
calendar.impact: The deadline for December shipper nominations, and the last date a December apportionment judgment call can be registered for the prediction record.

calendar.title: OPEC+ ministerial meeting on the 2027 framework
calendar.impact: The wider group meets to set the 2027 production framework, with the fourth quarter capacity review setting the baselines for 2027 quotas.
